For the periodic cellulation in [[def-qc-tqc-periodic-square-cellulation]],
put one qubit on each edge, ordered lexicographically by $(i,j)$ and then with
horizontal before vertical edges. The physical Hilbert space is
$\mathcal H_L=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes E}$, where $E$ is the edge set. For an
edge $e$, write $X_e$ and $Z_e$ for the corresponding one-qubit Pauli acting
on that tensor factor and as the identity on every other factor. Define the
star and plaquette checks by

$$A_{i,j}=X_{h_{i-1,j}}X_{h_{i,j}}X_{v_{i,j-1}}X_{v_{i,j}},\qquad B_{i,j}=Z_{h_{i,j}}Z_{v_{i+1,j}}Z_{h_{i,j+1}}Z_{v_{i,j}}.$$

All indices are in $\mathbb Z_L$.

All star and plaquette checks of [[def-qc-tqc-toric-checks]] commute. The
product of all stars is the identity, and the product of all plaquettes is
the identity.

For $L\ge3$, the $L^2$ star-support vectors in $\mathbb F_2^E$ have span
dimension $L^2-1$, and their only relation is their total sum. The $L^2$
face-boundary vectors have the same span dimension and their only relation
is their total sum. The dual-face incidence statement has the same rank.

derivations.claim: A product of retained checks with identity binary support must have zero X support and zero Z support separately. By [F3], this forces the selected star subset and plaquette subset both to be empty, so the retained checks are independent. By [F1] and [F2] they are commuting Hermitian involutions. For a retained check $g_a$ and sign $s_a$, put $p_{a,s_a}=(I+(-1)^{s_a}g_a)/2$. Direct expansion using $g_a^*=g_a$ and $g_a^2=I$ gives $p_{a,s_a}^*=p_{a,s_a}$ and $p_{a,s_a}^2=p_{a,s_a}$. The checks commute, so their factors commute; hence $P_s$ is a self-adjoint idempotent, thus an orthogonal projection.

If $s\ne t$, choose an index $a$ with $s_a\ne t_a$. Then $p_{a,s_a}p_{a,t_a}=(I-g_a^2)/4=0$, so $P_sP_t=0$. Summing over all sign strings and distributing the finite product gives $\sum_sP_s=\prod_a(p_{a,0}+p_{a,1})=I$. Thus the ranges are pairwise orthogonal and their direct sum is the whole Hilbert space; zero projections are allowed.

By [F2], the omitted star is the product of all retained stars, so on $\operatorname{ran}P_s$ its eigenvalue is the product of their signs; the product of the eigenvalues over all stars is therefore $+1$. A finite list of signs in $\{+1,-1\}$ has product $+1$ exactly when it contains an even number of minus signs. The same argument for the omitted plaquette gives even m-defect parity. The projectors therefore decompose the register into the stated full-check syndrome sectors.

is their total sum. The dual-face incidence statement has the same rank.

For a nonzero vector $\psi$ that is a simultaneous eigenvector of all toric
checks, its **e syndrome** is the set of vertices $q$ for which
$A_q\psi=-\psi$, and its **m syndrome** is the set of faces $f$ for which
$B_f\psi=-\psi$. A violated star is called an e defect and a violated
plaquette is called an m defect. These are finite stabilizer-syndrome labels;
the names do not assume that a material contains localized physical
quasiparticles.

The word **syndrome** follows the check-eigenvalue convention of
[[def-qc-stabilizer-syndrome-and-logical-operators]].

The checks are Hermitian involutions, as verified below; thus their
eigenvalues on any nonzero simultaneous eigenvector are indeed signs.

Let $Z_1$ be the space of primal edge chains with even incidence at every
vertex, and let $B_1$ be the span of the face boundaries. Then $B_1\subseteq
Z_1$, the quotient $Z_1/B_1$ has dimension two, and the two winding
parities give coordinates on that quotient. The same statement holds for
dual edge chains, with dual vertex boundaries in place of face boundaries.
The horizontal loop $\gamma_h=\sum_i h_{i,0}$ has winding pair $(1,0)$,
and the vertical loop $\gamma_v=\sum_j v_{0,j}$ has pair $(0,1)$; their dual
counterparts give the corresponding basis of the dual quotient.
